title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 1
paragraphs: Aristagoras, then, after having caused Ionia to revolt, thus ended his life; and meanwhile Histiaeus, the tyrant of Miletus, having been let go by Darius, had arrived at Sardis. When he came from Susa, Artaphrenes, governor of Sardis, asked him for what reason he supposed the Ionians had revolted; and Histiaeus said that he could not tell, and moreover expressed wonder at what had happened, pretending he knew nothing of the state of affairs. Then Artaphrenes, seeing that he was dissembling and knowing the truth about the revolt, said: “It stands with you, Histiaeus, in this way in these matters: this shoe was stitched by you, and put on by Aristagoras.”
